correctness.rationale: For generic central hyperplanes of [-1,1]^4, a section vertex is a unique crossed cube edge. Sorting |u_i| shows all 16 corner signs give exactly 8 crossings if the largest dominates the other three, otherwise 12; independent integer-sign examples corroborate. A fixed one of 32 edges crosses with probability P(|G1|>|G2+G3+G4|)=P(|C|>sqrt3)=1/3 by Gaussian symmetry and the exact Cauchy law, giving E f0=32/3 and hence weights 1/3 and 2/3. Genericity makes the 3-polytope simple; 2f1=3f0 and Euler give claimed full vectors. Measure-zero tie cases are explicitly excluded; finite enumeration/simulation cannot prove Haar weights.
residual_risks: Proof depends on standard cited external lemma(s) where identified; numerical checks are diagnostic not certificates.

value.rationale: The 4-cube is a canonical finite polytope and Haar central sections form a natural stochastic geometry ensemble. The complete joint f-vector law, not just mean face counts, and its sharp normal-coordinate phase rule are useful exact benchmarks for section combinatorics. Being finite-dimensional is not itself a demerit.
